deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a space with a global stratification by closed pieces X_i (i in a poset I), with X_h ∩ X_i a union of X_l for l ≤ h,i. Write \dot X_i = ∪_{k<i} X_k and X_i^* = X_i \ \dot X_i for the open stratum. For i ≤ j, \bar V_{ij} is a closed tubular neighbourhood of X_i inside X_j. R_{ij} is the union of the X_h with h<j and X_h ⊅ X_i, and \dot V_{ij} = \bar V_{ij} ∩ R_{ij}. Formula (4) of the previous page gives R_{ij} ∩ X_i = \dot X_i.

This page.
(5) V_{ij} = \bar V_{ij} \ \dot V_{ij}. This removes from the tube the parts lying over the lower strata that do not contain X_i.
(6) Hence V_{ij} ∩ X_i = X_i \ \dot X_i = X_i^*. So V_{ij} is a tubular neighbourhood of the open stratum X_i^* inside X_j.
(7) V_{ij}^* = \bar V_{ij} \ ∪_{k<j}(X_k ∩ \bar V_{ij}) = \bar V_{ij} \ \dot X_j = V_{ij} ∩ X_j^*. For i<j this is the 'deleted' tube: the part of the tube lying in the open stratum X_j^*. It no longer meets X_i.
(8) For i=j everything collapses: \bar V_{ii} = X_i, \dot V_{ii} = \dot X_i, and V_{ii} = V_{ii}^* = X_i^*.
(9) The 'building blocks' for a first step of the construction are the spans X_j^* ← V_{ij}^* → V_{ij} → X_i^*. The first two maps are inclusions. The last map is the 'âme' (soul), i.e. the tube projection or retraction onto the core stratum. The blocks include the open strata X_i^* as the case i=j.

Purpose. This is the start of a 'dévissage' of a stratified space, or stratified topos, into elementary pieces (open strata, tubes, deleted tubes), from which the space should be reconstructed by gluing. On the next page Grothendieck says these pieces are too general. He proposes restricting to j an immediate successor of i, where under equisingularity hypotheses V_{ij}^* is a bundle over X_i^* with fibre R × C_{ij}, C_{ij} a compact manifold (the link).
errors: (6) silently uses \bar V_{ij} ∩ X_i = X_i, i.e. that the tube contains its core, together with (4); this is implicit but fine.
The second equality in (7) needs R_{ij} ⊂ \dot X_j, which holds since R_{ij} is a union of X_h with h<j. Then V_{ij} ∩ X_j^* = \bar V_{ij} \ (R_{ij} ∪ \dot X_j) = \bar V_{ij} \ \dot X_j. Correct.
The arrow V_{ij} → X_i^* ('âme') is not an inclusion but a retraction. It presupposes extra structure (a tube projection) not yet defined in the text.
Whether V_{ij} is actually open in X_j depends on \bar V_{ij} being a neighbourhood; the word describing it ('voisinage ... entourant') is not fully legible.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine definitional manipulations setting up tubes and deleted tubes as gluing pieces for a stratified space. The idea matches Thom–Mather control data and Grothendieck's own published Esquisse programme on dévissage. Nothing beyond standard material appears on this page; the more interesting remark (restricting to successor pairs, link bundles) is on the next page.
